OpenCode Warden

A comprehensive security plugin for OpenCode that intercepts tool calls to detect secrets, redact sensitive data, evaluate safety risks, block access to sensitive files, and maintain a complete audit trail.

## Compatibility Warden's version is independent of the OpenCode **host** version. Choose the Warden line that matches your host's plugin API: | OpenCode host | Warden plugin | Status | |---|---|---| | **OpenCode 1.x** (V1 plugin API) | **1.3.0**, pinned exactly | Last Warden release for OpenCode 1.x. Published with `@opencode-ai/plugin` `^1.2.0`. **Do not install Warden 2.0.0 on OpenCode 1.x.** | | **OpenCode 2.0.0–2.0.17** | **2.0.0** | **Below the declared supported floor (2.0.18); not verified.** Warden loads with a warning and keeps protections installed, but host compatibility is not guaranteed. | | **OpenCode 2.0.18–2.0.28** | **2.0.0** | **Supported floor.** Bounded runtime validation of the built plugin with local mocks passed on 2.0.18, including the untyped per-call block path. Clean typed `Tool.Error` vetoes require 2.0.29+. | | **OpenCode 2.0.29+** | **2.0.0** | Supported. The typed per-call veto mapping introduced in 2.0.29 is source/package-verified; **not runtime-probed on a 2.0.29 or 2.1.4 binary**. See [Verification status](#runtime-boundaries). | OpenCode 2.x is the target line for Warden 2.0.0, but **not every 2.x host is verified**. The minimum declared floor is 2.0.18. Warden does not claim that all OpenCode 2.x versions are certified. **Bounded runtime results on 2.0.18** (isolated run of the built 2.0.0 with local mocks): config precedence and inline fallback, invalid-config lockdown, V2 `path`/`shell`/ `subagent` blocking, write/read/error redaction, outbound tool-result redaction and policy injection, global shell backstop, evaluator and output-sanitizer outage blocking in `warn` mode, explicit `llm.enabled: false` deterministic mode, `session.update({ permissions })` preservation and application, server RPC/SSE notification delivery, and compaction policy injection plus redaction with a valid summary. These results do **not** certify every host behavior and were not run on 2.1.4. A bounded 2.0.18 secret-write replay passed with the structural tool-call-input projection: exit 0 / `PROBE_DONE`, the file contained `[REDACTED]`, and the next request had `rawHasDKey:false`, `historyHasDKey:false`, and the policy present. A bounded 2.0.18 title/generate replay also passed: the tool-less title request had no policy, sent `[REDACTED]` instead of the raw key, and persisted `Replay Title` with exit 0; the public generate request had the policy and normal tools, sent redacted text, and returned `PROBE_DONE`. These replays are bounded validation, not certification of every behavior, and do not scrub at-rest input. Live rendered TUI toasts and the 2.0.29+/2.1.4 binaries remain untested; the structured-output content path passed at runtime, while the content-less fallback branch is unit-test only. ## Features - **65 active built-in detection patterns** across 11 categories — API keys, credentials, private keys, PII, cloud provider secrets, Docker, Kubernetes, and more (66 defined; `pii-ip-address` is off by default) - **V2-native tool vocabulary** — policies use `shell`, `subagent`, and `path`; legacy `bash`, `task`, and `filePath` configs and callers remain accepted as aliases. `patch` inputs are inspected through every `patchText` add/update/delete/move target - **Optional user prompt scanning** — opt-in via `scanUserPrompts: true`. When enabled, incoming prompt text plus attachment metadata (file URI/name/description, agent/skill names, mentions) is scanned before it reaches the LLM; prompts containing detected secrets are blocked and never persisted. File contents are deliberately not read. Disabled by default due to upstream TUI limitations on how blocked prompts are surfaced. - **LLM-powered safety evaluation** across 10 risk dimensions (exfiltration, destruction, privilege escalation, and more) - **LLM-enhanced output sanitization** — catches context-dependent secrets that regex alone misses - **Outbound request scanning** — before provider dispatch, `session.context` redacts supported system/message/tool-result text and compaction requests, and injects the security policy as a per-request system part. `session.generate` reuses the same policy, blocked-tool restrictions, and scanning as a primary request; the tool-less `session.title` request gets deterministic redaction without policy injection so title output is preserved. Tool-call ids/names and provider metadata are preserved; historical tool-call input strings are structurally redacted in the request projection, while file/media identifiers are scanned read-only and a detection withholds the request - **File path blocking** with glob patterns — prevents access to `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, kubeconfig, tfstate, and other sensitive files - **Global shell backstop** — every shell creation, including the user's own terminals/background shells, is checked against the file blocklist and write-protection lists. This is broader than agent-only enforcement and is intentional - **Write-protection** for read-only-but-never-modified files (logs, state) — read allowed, writes blocked deterministically including via shell redirections (`>`, `>>`, `tee`, `truncate`) - **Per-path redaction exemptions** — keep legitimate API keys in source code (client libraries, config templates) without Warden rewriting them to `[REDACTED]`. Covers `write`/`edit`/`patch`, `read`, shell redirections/reads, outbound context results, and SSH/SCP/rsync/rclone operations. Supports host-scoped entries (e.g. `host:web-*:/etc/myapp/**`) for remote-only exemptions - **Configurable redaction scope** — disable write-time redaction (`redactOnWrite`), or kill all redaction globally (`redactionEnabled`), without losing file blocking or safety evaluation - **Environment variable sanitization** — strips secrets from the shell environment before they reach tool calls - **Session deny rules (defense in depth)** — literal blocked tools and literal absolute blocklist/write-protected paths are also translated into session-scoped deny rules where OpenCode can express them exactly. Warden's primary hooks remain authoritative; configured glob/relative paths and shell path policy are intentionally not translated - **SSH-only mode** — monitor only remote commands (ssh, scp, sftp, rsync, rclone) while bypassing all local operations - **7 built-in tools** — dashboard, reports, audit queries, dry-run evaluation, config view, and rule management. Plugin tools use OpenCode's Code Mode by default, so the agent invokes them through `execute` (for example `tools.security_help`), not the native provider tool list - **Three-layer rule architecture** — builtin, user-managed, and AI-managed detection rules - **Customizable prompts** — replace any LLM prompt via config using `{{variableName}}` templates - **Zero-config operation** — works out of the box with sensible defaults, no LLM required - **Comprehensive audit logging** — JSON-line log files with rotation, verbosity levels, and session statistics - **Configurable action modes** — auto-block, user-prompted permission, or warn-only for both input safety and output sanitization. When the LLM is enabled, an outage still blocks input safety and non-`pass` output paths regardless of the configured mode ## Installation ### Prerequisites - **OpenCode 2.x** for Warden **2.0.0**. The declared supported floor is **OpenCode 2.0.18** (`@opencode/plugin` `^2.0.18`). Development and type-checking use the 2.1.4 SDK; the peer range expresses the 2.0.18 API floor that Warden's used surface is verified against. Hosts on 2.0.0–2.0.17 are below the floor and load with a warning while keeping protections installed. On 2.0.18–2.0.28, Warden blocks per call through the older untyped rejection path exercised on 2.0.18; clean typed `Tool.Error` vetoes require 2.0.29+. Neither the 2.0.29 nor the 2.1.4 binary has been runtime-probed. - **OpenCode 1.x** requires Warden **1.3.0** (pinned). Warden 2.0.0 uses the V2 plugin API and is not a drop-in replacement on a V1 host. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) runtime (OpenCode uses Bun for plugins) ### Install Warden 2.0.0 on OpenCode 2.x Add the pinned package to the `plugin` array in your OpenCode configuration. Installing by **package name** is the supported form; OpenCode resolves the published `exports` correctly: **Global** (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) — applies to all projects: ```json { "plugin": ["opencode-warden@2.0.0"] } ``` **Project-level** (`./opencode.json`) — applies to a single project: ```json { "plugin": ["opencode-warden@2.0.0"] } ``` You may omit `@2.0.0` to track the newest release, but pinning avoids surprise upgrades. OpenCode installs npm plugins automatically with Bun at startup. ### Install Warden 1.3.0 on OpenCode 1.x OpenCode 1.x uses the V1 plugin API. Pin the last Warden release for that line: ```json { "plugin": ["opencode-warden@1.3.0"] } ``` Use the same `plugin` array in either the global or project `opencode.json`. Warden 1.3.0 is published on npm with peer dependency `@opencode-ai/plugin` `^1.2.0`. **Do not install `opencode-warden@2.0.0` on OpenCode 1.x.** An unpinned install can resolve differently after a new release is tagged `latest`, so pin `1.3.0` explicitly. For the 1.3.0 configuration reference, use the [v1.3.0 README](https://github.com/toreuyar/opencode-warden/blob/v1.3.0/README.md) and [v1.3.0 example config](https://github.com/toreuyar/opencode-warden/blob/v1.3.0/opencode-warden.example.json) rather than this 2.0.0 documentation. ### Install from Source If you prefer to run from source (for development or customization): ```bash # Warden 2.0.0 for OpenCode 2.x git clone https://github.com/toreuyar/opencode-warden.git cd opencode-warden bun install bun run build # Warden 1.3.0 for OpenCode 1.x git clone --branch v1.3.0 https://github.com/toreuyar/opencode-warden.git cd opencode-warden bun install ``` > **Local-directory entrypoint:** on OpenCode 2.x, when a 2.0.0 `plugin` entry > points at a local **directory**, OpenCode probes `/server` and > `/index`. It does not read the package's `package.json` `main`/`exports`, so a checkout that only has > `dist/index.js` loads Warden silently as a no-op. This was reproduced on > 2.0.18 (the supported floor); the same resolver source is present in 2.1.4. > Use the package name after a normal npm install, or create root entry files > from the build: ```bash cp dist/index.js index.js # required — server/plugin entrypoint cp dist/rpc.js rpc.js # only for the RPC notification surface cp dist/tui.js tui.js # only for the TUI companion ``` Then register the plugin by adding its **absolute path** to `opencode.json`: ```json { "plugin": [ "/absolute/path/to/opencode-warden" ] } ``` Re-run `bun run build` and re-copy the files after source changes. The root `index.js` is what the local-directory resolver loads; `dist/index.js` alone is not enough. > **Note**: The path must be absolute (e.g., `/home/user/opencode-warden` on Linux, `/Users/user/opencode-warden` on macOS). A wrong or non-existent path will cause OpenCode to hang on startup. ### Alternative: Plugin Directory You can also copy the built plugin **files** into OpenCode's plugin directories: - **Global**: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` - **Project-level**: `.opencode/plugins/` Place the built entrypoint as a file (for example `index.js`, plus `rpc.js` and `tui.js` when those surfaces are needed) rather than a package subdirectory. Files placed in these directories are loaded automatically. ## Quick Start Warden works with **zero configuration**. Once installed, it immediately: 1. Blocks access to sensitive files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, etc.) 2. Scans and redacts secrets in tool inputs and outputs using 65 active regex patterns 3. Sanitizes environment variables before they reach shell commands 4. Scans outbound model requests and compaction requests, and injects the security policy per request 5. Applies a global shell backstop to agent and user shells 6. Logs all security events to `.opencode/warden/audit.log` 7. Provides 7 built-in tools for real-time visibility and rule management through OpenCode Code Mode (`execute` → `tools.security_*`) 8. Sends sanitized alerts through the TUI/RPC companion when `notifications` is enabled (fixed event kinds + bounded tool/count only; no paths, arguments, explanations, or output). Notifications are UX-only and never affect enforcement To enable LLM-powered safety evaluation (recommended for production use), create a config file: ```json { "llm": { "enabled": true, "baseUrl": "http://localhost:11434/v1", "model": "your-model-name" } } ``` Place this file at `.opencode/opencode-warden.json` in your project root or `~/.config/opencode/opencode-warden.json` for global settings. ### Configuration precedence and failure behavior - Configuration is merged as defaults → global file → project file. Arrays are replaced, not appended. - Inline `ctx.options` are a fallback only when **neither** the global nor project config file exists. If either file exists, inline options are ignored entirely, even when that file is invalid or unreadable — the file always wins. - Invalid or unreadable configuration does **not** unload Warden. Warden installs a fail-closed lockdown that denies permissions, vetoes tool execution, withholds tool output, and blocks prompts, model requests, compaction, and shell creation until the configuration is fixed and OpenCode is restarted. - With the LLM enabled, an unreachable/misconfigured evaluator or sanitizer blocks the operation regardless of `actionMode` (`warn` and `permission` do not allow an outage through). The explicit `llm.enabled: false` mode is deterministic-only and does not block because of LLM absence. - A 2.x runtime below 2.0.18 produces a warning but keeps all protections installed. On 2.0.18–2.0.28, Warden also warns that typed per-call vetoes require 2.0.29+; blocking uses the older untyped path. Warden never refuses setup for a version mismatch, because a failed plugin setup would leave the host entirely unprotected. This does not extend V1 compatibility to OpenCode 1.x. ### Runtime boundaries - **Hook ordering:** OpenCode runs hooks in registration order with no priority API. Later plugins observe earlier mutations, so Warden cannot guarantee its mutations are final. Treat the host and all loaded plugins as trusted, and load Warden last where possible; registration order alone is not a security boundary. - **Ephemeral context redaction:** outbound redaction on `session.context`, `session.generate`, `session.title`, and `session.compaction` mutates per-request projections, not stored history. History remains unchanged. Tool-call ids/names, message metadata, and `providerMetadata` are preserved. Historical tool-call input strings are structurally redacted in the projection with ids/names/keys/shape preserved; file/media identifiers and provider-signed/encrypted text are never rewritten, and a required change there aborts the request (fail-closed) instead of corrupting the provider payload. Signature-bearing text can therefore cause a rejected request rather than a silently altered one. - **Secret-bearing writes and at-rest input:** `write`/`edit`/`patch` input redaction protects the file that is written, but the host persists the model's original tool-call input before `tool.execute.before` runs. The next dispatch structurally redacts detected strings in that historical input for the provider request, so the secret is not forwarded; Warden does **not** rewrite the persisted session store, so the raw input remains at rest. Provider-signed/encrypted or unsupported input shapes abort instead of being rewritten. `redactOnWrite: false` and `redactionExemptPaths` exempt those historical inputs and allow the secret through, so they are not a secure remedy. Prefer not to route real secrets through model-authored writes. A bounded 2.0.18 replay passed with this structural projection (exit 0, next request redacted, policy present); raw pre-hook input remains at rest, and this is not a 2.0.18 or 2.1.4 certification. - **Auxiliary request coverage:** `session.generate` is scanned with the same policy append, blocked-tool removal, and outbound redaction as a primary request. `session.title` is tool-less and deliberately receives no policy injection; it is scanned and redacted deterministically, and the title result is preserved. A bounded 2.0.18 replay passed both surfaces (title sent `[REDACTED]` and persisted `Replay Title`; generate sent redacted text and returned `PROBE_DONE`). No actual external provider, 2.1.4 binary, or live rendered TUI was used. - **Verification status:** bounded runtime validation was performed on **OpenCode 2.0.18** (the declared floor) with the built Warden 2.0.0, loaded through a root `index.js` entrypoint and using local mocks rather than an external provider. It passed config precedence and inline fallback, invalid-config lockdown, V2 path/shell/subagent blocking, write/read/error redaction, bounded secret-write replay with structural tool-call-input projection redaction (exit 0, next request redacted, policy present), outbound tool-result redaction and policy injection, title and generate replay (title redacted with no policy and preserved `Replay Title`; generate redacted with policy/tools and returned `PROBE_DONE`), shell backstop, evaluator/sanitizer outage blocking in `warn`, explicit `llm.enabled: false` deterministic mode, `session.update({ permissions })` preservation and application, server RPC/SSE notification delivery, and compaction policy injection plus redaction with a valid summary. These are bounded results, not a certification of every host behavior. They were not run on 2.1.4. The **typed per-call veto mapping** (`Tool.Error`) was introduced in `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.29 and is source/package-verified there and in 2.1.4; on 2.0.18–2.0.28 the host uses the older untyped per-call rejection path, which the 2.0.18 validation exercised. **Live rendered TUI toasts remain untested** (server RPC/SSE delivery passed on 2.0.18). Structured output passed at runtime through the host-normalized content path; the content-less structured fallback branch is unreachable on 2.0.18 and remains unit-test only. - **Notifications:** UI alerts are UX-only. Enforcement decisions, blocks, and audit records do not depend on a toast or TUI connection succeeding. ## Versioning and upgrading to 2.0.0 **Warden 2.0.0 is the plugin version.** It is separate from the OpenCode host version. Warden 2.0.0 targets the OpenCode V2 plugin API with a supported host floor of **OpenCode 2.0.18** (`@opencode/plugin` peer `^2.0.18`, developed and type-checked against 2.1.4). References to OpenCode 2.0.18 elsewhere describe the declared floor and the bounded-validation host, not the Warden version. Typed per-call `Tool.Error` vetoes are available from host 2.0.29; earlier supported hosts (2.0.18–2.0.28) still block per call through the untyped path. ### Upgrade checklist 1. **Check the host line first.** On **OpenCode 1.x**, do **not** upgrade to Warden 2.0.0. Pin `opencode-warden@1.3.0` (see [Compatibility](#compatibility)). 2. **Upgrade OpenCode first** on the 2.x line. Use at least a 2.0.18 host. For clean typed per-call tool vetoes, use 2.0.29+. Hosts on 2.0.0–2.0.17 are below the floor and load with a warning; 2.0.18–2.0.28 load with a typed-veto advisory and block through the older untyped path exercised on 2.0.18. 3. **Upgrade the plugin** to `opencode-warden@2.0.0` and restart OpenCode. 4. **Remove obsolete tool entries.** V2 has no `list` tool, so `excludedTools` now defaults to `[]`; delete any `"list"` entry. 5. **Keep legacy config names if you prefer.** `bash`, `task`, and `filePath` remain accepted aliases for `shell`, `subagent`, and `path`. New configs should use the V2 names. 6. **Review LLM settings.** The default request timeout is `0` (no timeout). Set an explicit positive `llm.timeout` when enabling the LLM, and remember that an enabled-but-unreachable evaluator now blocks even in `warn`/`permission`. 7. **Check notification delivery.** Alerts use the event-only TUI/RPC contract. If you run without the TUI companion, enforcement and audit logging continue but UI alerts may be absent. ### Breaking changes and behavior changes - **OpenCode 1.x is not supported by Warden 2.0.0.** The legacy plugin API and `chat.message`/`shell.env`/`permission.ask` integration points are replaced by the V2 hook families. OpenCode 1.x users should stay on the pinned 1.3.0 release. - Invalid or unreadable configuration installs an active lockdown instead of unloading Warden. Inline `ctx.options` are used only when neither config file exists. - An LLM outage is fail-closed for input safety and non-`pass` output paths regardless of `actionMode`. Explicit `llm.enabled: false` remains deterministic-only. - Outbound redaction on `session.context`, `session.generate`, `session.title`, and `session.compaction` is ephemeral: it protects the request projection, not stored conversation history. The raw pre-hook tool-call input for a secret-bearing write remains in the session store; redaction of the outbound projection is not at-rest scrubbing. - Outbound scanning now covers `session.generate` with the same policy and tool restrictions as a primary request. The tool-less `session.title` request is redacted deterministically without policy injection so title output is preserved. - Configured **local-directory** installs need a root `index.js` (plus `rpc.js`/ `tui.js` when used); the resolver does not read a local package's `main`/ `exports`. Installing by package name uses the published exports normally. - The global shell backstop also covers the user's own terminals and background shells. Dynamic targets that need shell expansion are skipped deterministically. - Default safety evaluation now includes `patch` and `read`; output sanitization uses `shell` instead of `bash` (the legacy alias still works). - Session deny-rule sync replaces the host ruleset non-atomically; it is defense in depth, not the authoritative guard. See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for the complete 2.0.0 release notes. ## Documentation - [**Configuration**](docs/configuration.md) — Configuration hierarchy, all option tables, complete example, and minimal config presets - [**How It Works**](docs/how-it-works.md) — Hook pipeline, detection engine, LLM integration, customizing prompts, action modes, and permission system integration - [**Built-in Tools**](docs/tools.md) — All 7 tools documented: `security_help`, `security_dashboard`, `security_report`, `security_audit`, `security_evaluate`, `security_config`, `security_rules` - [**Detection Patterns**](docs/detection-patterns.md) — Full pattern tables for all categories: API keys, credentials, private keys, Docker, Kubernetes, cloud providers, and PII - [**Use Cases**](docs/use-cases.md) — 8 example configurations covering solo dev, team projects, CI/CD, SSH-only mode, enterprise, and more - [**Audit Logging & Environment Sanitization**](docs/audit-logging.md) — Log format, rotation, querying, and environment variable sanitization - [**Changelog**](CHANGELOG.md) — Release notes and the 2.0.0 upgrade/breaking-change summary ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. # Changelog

All notable user-facing changes to OpenCode Warden are recorded here. The
project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Release notes for
versions before 2.0.0 are available in the git history and release tags.

## [2.0.0] — 2026-10-24

Warden **2.0.0** is the plugin release that ports the project to OpenCode's V2
plugin API. It is not an OpenCode host version: the supported host floor is
**OpenCode 2.0.18** (`@opencode/plugin` peer `^2.0.18`; developed and
type-checked against the 2.1.4 SDK). Typed per-call `Tool.Error` vetoes require
host **2.0.29+**; 2.0.18–2.0.28 block through the older untyped per-call
rejection path.

### Compatibility

| OpenCode host | Warden plugin | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode 1.x (V1 plugin API) | **1.3.0**, pinned exactly | Last Warden release for OpenCode 1.x; published with `@opencode-ai/plugin` `^1.2.0`. Warden 2.0.0 is not compatible with a V1 host. |
| OpenCode 2.0.0–2.0.17 | **2.0.0** | Below the declared 2.0.18 floor; **not verified**. Warden loads with a warning and keeps protections installed. |
| OpenCode 2.0.18–2.0.28 | **2.0.0** | **Declared supported floor**, bounded runtime-validated on 2.0.18 with local mocks. Blocking works through the older untyped per-call rejection path. Clean typed `Tool.Error` vetoes require 2.0.29+. |
| OpenCode 2.0.29+ | **2.0.0** | Supported. The typed veto mapping introduced in 2.0.29 is source/package-verified; **not runtime-probed on a 2.0.29 or 2.1.4 binary**. |

OpenCode 1.x users should install the exact V1-compatible release:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-warden@1.3.0"]
}
```

Do not use an unpinned `"opencode-warden"` entry on an OpenCode 1.x host: once
2.0.0 is the npm `latest` tag, that entry resolves to an incompatible plugin.
For 2.x hosts, pin `"opencode-warden@2.0.0"` (or intentionally track latest).

### Runtime validation (2.0.18)

Bounded, isolated validation of the built 2.0.0 ran on **OpenCode 2.0.18**
(the declared floor, using local mocks and loaded through a root `index.js`) and
passed: configuration precedence and
inline fallback; invalid-config lockdown with no provider dispatch; V2
`path`/`shell`/`subagent` blocking; write, read, and error-result redaction;
outbound tool-result redaction and policy injection; global shell backstop;
enabled evaluator and output-sanitizer outage blocking in `warn`; explicit
`llm.enabled: false` deterministic mode; `session.update({ permissions })`
preservation and application; server RPC/SSE notification delivery; and
compaction policy injection plus redaction with a valid summary.

The bounded run exercised the untyped per-call rejection path available on
2.0.18. The typed `Tool.Error` veto mapping was introduced in
`@opencode/plugin` 2.0.29 and is source/package-verified, not runtime-probed on a
2.0.29 or 2.1.4 binary. Live rendered TUI toasts
were not tested; only server RPC/SSE delivery was. A bounded 2.0.18 secret-write
replay passed with the structural tool-call-input projection: exit 0 /
`PROBE_DONE`, the file contained `[REDACTED]`, and the next request had
`rawHasDKey:false`, `historyHasDKey:false`, and the policy present. That replay
does not scrub at-rest input. A bounded 2.0.18 title/generate
replay also passed: the tool-less title request had no policy, sent
`[REDACTED]` instead of the raw key, and persisted `Replay Title` with exit 0;
the public generate request had the policy and normal tools, sent redacted text,
and returned `PROBE_DONE`. Structured output was redacted at runtime through the
host-normalized content path; the content-less structured fallback branch is
unreachable on 2.0.18 and remains unit-test only. These results are bounded
validation, not a certification of every host behavior.

### Added

- **V2 hook coverage** for `session.prompt`, `tool.execute.before`,
  `shell.create.before`, `permission.evaluate`, `tool.execute.after`,
  `session.context`, `session.generate`, `session.title`, and
  `session.compaction`, plus session lifecycle event subscriptions.
- **Outbound and compaction DLP.** Before provider dispatch, Warden appends the
  security policy as a per-request system part and redacts supported outbound
  system/message/tool-result text. `session.generate` receives the same policy,
  blocked-tool restrictions, and scanning as a primary request. `session.title`
  is tool-less: it receives deterministic redaction without policy injection,
  preserving title quality. Compaction requests receive the same deterministic
  treatment. Redaction applies to the request projection only; stored history is
  not rewritten.
- **Tool-surface enforcement.** Blocked tools are removed from request tool
  definitions and from the registered tool list through `tool.transform`,
  including tools added by the same transform. Custom Warden tools are
  registered through the V2 editor rather than the legacy tool map.
- **Global shell backstop.** Every shell creation, including user terminals and
  background shells, is checked against the blocked/write-protected path
  policy. Environment stripping and value redaction run in the same hook.
- **Prompt attachment-metadata scanning.** Opt-in prompt scanning now covers
  text plus file URI/name/description, agent/skill names, and mention text.
  Attachment file contents are not read. Blocking aborts prompt admission.
- **Session deny rules (defense in depth).** Literal blocked tools and literal
  absolute blocked/write-protected paths are translated into session-scoped
  deny rules where OpenCode can express them exactly.
- **TUI/RPC notifications.** Hook alerts use a strict event-only contract with a
  closed kind and bounded tool/count metadata. The optional TUI companion
  renders fixed copy. Delivery is UX-only and never changes enforcement.
- **Session lifecycle wiring** for `session.created`, `session.deleted`, and
  `session.permissions`, including deny-rule cache invalidation and session-state
  cleanup.

### Changed

- **Configuration failures are an active lockdown.** Invalid or unreadable
  configuration no longer risks a failed plugin setup. Warden installs
  deny-all/withhold-all hooks and keeps them active until the configuration is
  fixed and OpenCode is restarted.
- **Inline configuration is a fallback only.** `ctx.options` are used only when
  neither the global nor the project config file exists. Any present file wins,
  even if that file is invalid or unreadable.
- **LLM outages are strictly fail-closed.** When the LLM is enabled,
  an unreachable, misconfigured, timed-out, or invalid evaluator/sanitizer
  blocks the operation regardless of `actionMode` — including `warn` and
  `permission`. Only explicit `llm.enabled: false` runs deterministic-only
  without outage blocking.
- **Output error handling.** Tool output, title, metadata, error messages, and
  error causes are sanitized. If an enabled sanitizer is unavailable for a tool
  in its list, output is withheld in `redact`/`warn` modes rather than released
  raw. `pass` remains an explicit detection-only debugging mode.
- **V2 tool vocabulary.** Defaults and policy use `shell`, `subagent`, and
  `path`; `bash`, `task`, and `filePath` remain accepted aliases. `patch`
  inputs are checked through every `patchText` add/update/delete/move target.
- **Default tool coverage.** Safety evaluation now defaults to `shell`, `write`,
  `edit`, `patch`, `read`, and `webfetch`; output sanitization defaults to
  `read`, `shell`, and `grep`. `excludedTools` now defaults to `[]` because V2
  has no `list` tool.

### Breaking changes and upgrade notes

- **OpenCode 1.x users must stay on Warden 1.3.0.** Warden 2.0.0 uses the V2
  plugin API and will not work as a V1 replacement.
- The supported host floor on the 2.x line is **OpenCode 2.0.18**
  (`@opencode/plugin` peer `^2.0.18`; development/type-checking uses 2.1.4).
  Hosts on 2.0.0–2.0.17 are below the floor and emit a warning while keeping
  protections installed. Hosts on 2.0.18–2.0.28 are supported and emit a
  typed-veto advisory: Warden blocks through the older untyped per-call
  rejection path exercised on 2.0.18, and typed `Tool.Error` vetoes require
  2.0.29+. Warden never refuses setup for a version mismatch; a
  failed setup would leave the host unprotected. Bounded 2.0.18 validation
  passed the cases above, but this is not a claim that every 2.x host is
  certified.
- Configured **local-directory** installs must provide a root `index.js`
  (`server.*` also works) and, when used, root `rpc.js`/`tui.js`. The host
  resolver probes those names instead of reading the local package's `main`/
  `exports`; a package directory without them loads silently as a no-op.
  Installing by package name resolves the published exports normally.
- Remove any `"list"` entry from `excludedTools`; it is obsolete and no longer
  matches a V2 tool.
- If you depend on raw toast text, migrate to the `opencode-warden.notifications`
  RPC contract. Notification events do not carry paths, arguments, output, or
  explanations.
- Audit and diagnostic files remain the durable record. A missing or slow TUI
  companion does not delay setup and does not weaken enforcement.
- The global shell backstop intentionally affects user-created shells, not only
  agent tool calls. Dynamic shell targets (for example unexpanded `$VAR` or
  backtick substitutions) cannot be resolved without executing the shell and are
  skipped by the deterministic backstop.

### Security boundaries and limitations

- **Hook ordering:** OpenCode runs hooks in registration order and has no
  priority API. A later plugin can observe or mutate earlier results, so Warden
  cannot guarantee its mutations are final. Treat the host and all loaded
  plugins as trusted, and load Warden last where possible.
- **Ephemeral redaction:** outbound redaction on `session.context`,
  `session.generate`, `session.title`, and `session.compaction` does not rewrite
  stored history. Tool-call IDs/names, message metadata, and `providerMetadata`
  are preserved. Historical tool-call input strings are structurally redacted in
  the request projection with keys/ids/names/shape preserved. File/media
  identifiers and provider-signed/encrypted text are never rewritten; a required
  rewrite aborts the request instead of corrupting provider pairing or
  signatures.
- **Secret-bearing writes:** write-time redaction protects the file, but the
  host persists the original tool-call input before `tool.execute.before`.
  Warden structurally redacts detected strings in that historical input for the
  next provider request, so the secret is not forwarded. The raw input remains at
  rest in the session store: projection redaction is not at-rest scrubbing.
  Provider-signed/encrypted or unsupported input shapes abort instead. Setting
  `redactOnWrite: false` or adding `redactionExemptPaths` exempts the historical
  input and allows the secret through; it is not a secure fix. A bounded 2.0.18
  secret-write replay passed (exit 0, next request redacted, policy present);
  raw pre-hook input remains at rest and this is not a broad certification.
- **Auxiliary requests:** `session.generate` uses the same policy append,
  blocked-tool removal, and outbound redaction as a primary request. The
  tool-less `session.title` request is redacted deterministically but receives no
  policy injection, preserving title output. Both passed a bounded 2.0.18
  local-mock replay (title sent `[REDACTED]` and persisted `Replay Title`;
  generate sent redacted text and returned `PROBE_DONE`). No external provider,
  2.1.4 binary, or live rendered TUI was used.
- **Media and provider payloads:** attachment file contents and binary/media
  bodies are not scanned by the outbound sanitizer. Coverage depends on the
  host exposing supported text/tool-result fields; unsupported shapes fail
  closed for the request.
- **Session permission sync:** `session.update({ permissions })` replaces the
  host ruleset and has no compare-and-set. Warden re-reads, merges, and
  re-reads before writing, which narrows but does not eliminate a concurrent
  update race. These rules are never the primary guard. Preservation and
  application passed on 2.0.18; newer-host behavior is source-verified only.
- **Code Mode tools:** plugin tools default to OpenCode Code Mode, so Warden's
  seven `security_*` tools are invoked through `execute` (`tools.security_*`),
  not listed in the native provider tool list. `blockedTools` removal still
  applies to the effective registry. Native direct visibility is not claimed.
- **Notification classification:** on 2.0.18 a blocked file read was emitted as
  RPC `kind: "denied"` rather than `"blocked"` because legacy toast text matched
  the denial classifier first. This is UX-only and does not change enforcement.
- **Audit durability:** audit writes are buffered (1 second or 10 entries). A
  short-lived `opencode run --standalone` process that exits immediately can
  leave a 0-byte audit file even though enforcement ran; long-lived servers
  flush normally. Enforcement is unaffected.
- **Runtime verification:** bounded runtime validation was performed on
  OpenCode 2.0.18 (the declared floor) with the built plugin loaded through a
  root `index.js` and local mocks.
  `session.update({ permissions })`, server RPC/SSE notification delivery, and
  compaction policy/redaction passed there, along with the untyped per-call
  block path. The typed `Tool.Error` veto mapping introduced in
  `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.29 (and the 2.1.4 hook shapes) is source/package-verified,
  not runtime-probed on a 2.0.29 or 2.1.4 binary.
  Live rendered TUI toasts remain untested. Structured output passed through the
  host-normalized content path; the content-less fallback branch is unit-test
  only.

### Documentation

- Added this changelog, an upgrade guide in the README, and refreshed the hook
  pipeline, audit/environment, detection-pattern, and use-case documentation for
  the V2 architecture.
